pass_fail_gate.rule: Every model name or identifier resolves to exactly one catalogue product ID and an approved configuration.
Every price, percentage, performance figure, duration and count matches a verified fact or a reproducible calculation.
A price in a title needs an approved offer record checked within 30 days, with configuration and currency.
Reject unsupported outcome claims: replaces staff, guaranteed ROI, proven safer, eliminates downtime.
The article contains an identifiable, evidence-based answer to the title's central question.
A title implying testing, ranking or measured performance links to evidence of exactly that kind.
Reject a title whose intent duplicates an existing page without a materially different answer.

claim_contract.title: Genisom L1 vs L1 EDU: One Decision, Two Invoices

title_system.numbers_in_titles: Prices and model names help with procurement intent and branded search; counts help only when the article carries the checklist; none of them rescue an article that does not deliver the promise.
title_system.price_rule: Price leads at most one title in five, and only where price is the buyer's actual question — a cost guide, a marginal-cost verdict, a verification-before-you-pay piece. Everywhere else the title leads with the decision, the constraint or the misconception, and the price lives in the body. A catalogue where every headline carries a number reads like a price list and stops being credible.

publication_gate.architecture: Verified product registry + versioned research packs → research agent → writing agent → audit agent → deterministic validation gate → release queue or repair/hold.

exception_path: Internal commercial offers, distribution authorisation, local compliance conclusions and genuine field-test claims need an authorised record or they are held. Human intervention is the exception mechanism, not the writing bottleneck.
